report:
Freshly started and inspected the current complete claim, four associated implementation files, six complete associated tests, and association metadata. All entries are ordinary; there are no TODO/N/A prerequisites or deferrals. This is a source assessment of the final current evidence, not a reuse of a previous approval. No source files were changed in this review and no tests were executed during this refresh; the coordinator owns central execution.

Completed-result requirement: observe::walk_symbol obtains function.body(db) and opens the returned body before traversing any types. walk_expr reads expr.ty from that completed tree and FrozenType::read converts it without a mutable inference context. Selection occurs on checked rows after check_crate; neither markers nor expected strings choose semantic candidates or introduce inference constraints. The correspondence search chooses among already checked source counterparts, not language resolution alternatives. compile/mod.rs passes only fixture/configuration/markers to compilation and consults expectation contents only after prepare succeeds in run. Expected presence controls validation, not semantic answers. The test completed_types_ignore_expected_text_and_use_later_constraints explicitly supplies incompatible invented bool and u64 expectations for the same unsuffixed literal, asserts both prepared results equal, and asserts u16 from its later local use/return constraint with empty diagnostics. This meaningfully detects early or expectation-driven type selection.

Completeness and failure requirement: source::walk recursively enumerates source expressions; walk_symbol matches them to the completed typed rows and records an invalid FrozenType::Missing row for absent or ambiguous correspondence rather than silently skipping it. collect checks validity and recursive type completeness before rendering and returns an error when a selected line has no completed expression. FrozenType::read maps InferVar to Missing; complete recursively checks tuple, named arguments, references, slices, arrays, function inputs/results and projection components. Missing cannot render as a plausible type. nested_inference_variables_are_not_completed_observations visibly asserts that a tuple containing an inference variable is incomplete and bool is complete. expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree asserts a line with no expression fails, alongside marker/expectation consistency checks. These tests, plus inspection of the invalid-row propagation, account for missing and unresolved observations. call_argument_types asserts the full selected path, literal and call set with fn(u16)->u32, u16 and u32; an omitted selected expression or invented type changes that snapshot.

Error-type qualification: FrozenType preserves Ty::Error as <error> while treating unresolved successful inference differently. explicit_error_types_are_observed_after_checking supplies an undefined name and a deliberate shared ERROR marker, asserts precisely one visible path observation with <error>, and asserts the unresolved diagnostic. Its assertions are on prepare output, so empty expectation values cannot satisfy them accidentally.

Coercion requirement: walk_expr recursively visits the child of NeverToAny before emitting a separate coercion row. Source correspondence excludes wrappers when finding the original expression and then appends associated coercion rows. It never overwrites the original type with the wrapper result. coercion_wrapper_follows_its_source_expression asserts literal 22 as u16, return 22 as ! and its coercion as u16, preserving both types and their order.

All essential harness dependencies for this assessment are already captured as associated whole-file fragments: compile/mod.rs (macro and prepare/run boundary), observe.rs (checking, correspondence, selection and traversal), source.rs (source enumeration), and types.rs (freezing/completeness/formatting). Complete inline test bodies and unit assertions were read from the fresh captured input. No outside helper source was used to infer an additional behavioral guarantee. The current implementation and six-test set adequately support every aspect of this anchor; no edits requested.
